features.link-reach: up to 600 km on the QSFP-DD ports (HIG Port Overview table)
features.op2-statistics: enabling the OP2 statistics counter disables ports 1, 17, 19 and 35 as service ports and reserves them for statistics, leaving 32 service ports (HIG Figures 9 and 11)
features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400GE QSFP-DD OpenZR+/ZR/SR8/FR4/LR4/ER4/DR4/DR4+/PLR4; 200GE QSFP56 SR4/FR4; 100GE QSFP28 SR4/LR4/ER4/ZR4 (datasheet compatible transceiver list)

features.zr-port-set: OpenZR+ and ZR are supported on the eighteen even-numbered ports, 0 to 34 - the upper row - which HIG Figure 10 shades in brown and names in the sentence above it

management.console: RJ45 RS-232 (the IOIO port) plus a micro-USB serial console
management.timing-support: Stratum 3E OCXO with optional holdover; ITU-T Synchronous Ethernet (SyncE); IEEE 1588v2 default, G.8265.1, G.8275.1, G.8275.2, SMPTE ST 2059-2, T-BC/OC, T-TC; Class C timing accuracy. NOS integration is necessary to activate the specific feature and ST 2059-2 requires an additional licence (the datasheet's own two asterisked qualifiers)

thermal.airflow: front-to-back (exhaust) only - the HIG states 'airflow direction is front-to-back' and the datasheet lists one fan and two supplies, all 'exhaust air flow'

No held figure shows this build seated in the chassis - see the ac-build-rear-face gap.

configs.description: The chassis as every held rear figure draws it - four FAN-808012-HC fans and two PSU-302-DESR 3000 W DC supplies, red handles and latches throughout, exhaust (front-to-back) airflow, and the thirty-eight traffic and management ports empty. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.

configs.description: Dual 3000 W -40 V to -72 V DC supplies (PSU-302-DESR, two-stud screw terminal block under a plastic cover) with FAN-808012-HC fans. This is the build both the HIG's rear elevation and the vendor rear render draw. The HIG rates the feed for operation up to 5000 m and notes a 150 A fast-acting fuse built into each supply; system maximum 1752 W on MSA optics and 2073 W with OpenZR+.

gaps.note: Every held image of this faceplate letters it S9610-36D: the S9611-36D HIG's own port-overview figures 8 to 11, the S9611-36D datasheet's front and rear views, and all three vendor renders. The S9611-36D and S9610-36D are a near-twin pair and UfiSpace has illustrated the S9611-36D's documents with the sibling's artwork. The silkscreen here prints S9611-36D on the reasoning that a router does not letter itself as a different product, which is a judgement and not a reading. Nothing else on the face is affected - the dimensions, port table, LED table and callouts in the guide are all written for the S9611-36D.
gaps.wanted: a photograph of a real S9611-36D front panel, or vendor faceplate artwork

gaps.note: The HIG's section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps, and stops. Nothing states what a port lamp means - link, activity, fault, or a lane aggregate - and no colour but the artwork's unlit green is shown. WHICH port each lamp belongs to is not in doubt (the printed triangle beside it points at its column), so every lamp carries a single `for:`; only the vocabulary is missing, and each lamp therefore keeps the component's plain off/on default. The two lamps above the SFP+ stack are the weaker case: they sit side by side above the upper cage rather than one per cage, and are assigned left-to-port-0 / right-to-port-1 from the '0 up-triangle / down-triangle 1' legend directly above them, which is a positional reading and not a stated mapping.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: Four features on the left-hand column are on the metal in every image and are named in no document. Two shallow round blind bosses, a small textured square window that reads like a mesh or a sensor, and a pair of short rounded slots under the beacon display. HIG Figure 4's callout list runs Reset, Beacon LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, USB, Micro USB, RJ45, System LED and 2 x SFP, and covers none of them. They are drawn as panel decor at their measured positions and given no part identity, because guessing one would put a name in the tree that no source supports.
gaps.wanted: a labelled front-panel figure, or a photograph of a real unit at close range

gaps.note: The HIG's Component Physical Information table gives the fan module 81 x 151.3 x 81.5 mm (W x D x H). The module seams in HIG Figure 4's rear elevation, which passes the aspect gate at 0.37%, sit on a 121.4 px pitch, i.e. 83.5 mm, and the vendor rear render puts the same seams on 291.3 px, i.e. 83.95 mm - so the drawn faces are about 2.7 mm further apart than the table's module is wide. The likely resolution is the S9321-64E's, where the same 808012 fan measures 81 in the table and 83.2 across the drawn flange: 81 is the body behind the flange and the face is wider. That is an inference and not something either document says, so the manifest seats the table's 81 mm module on the measured 83.7 mm pitch and draws the difference as chassis web, and this entry carries the disagreement.
gaps.wanted: a vendor mechanical drawing of FAN-808012, or a caliper on the FRU

gaps.note: This HIG dimensions the fan 81 x 151.3 x 81.5; the S9321-64E HIG, from which ufispace/fan-808012@1 was built, dimensions the same 808012 series 81 x 154.8 x 81.5 and weighs it 741 g against this guide's 737 g. Face size and height agree exactly and only the depth and weight differ, which is what a suffix change (-HC here, -HCE there) usually is. The component is reused unchanged because nothing on the modelled face depends on the 3.5 mm, and the configuration overrides the model string to FAN-808012-HC, which is the part this datasheet actually orders.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace fan ordering guide covering both suffixes

gaps.note: HIG section 8 says the router 'can be grounded from the router's case and/or the power supply units (PSUs)', and both rear images show what that means: an earth symbol and a round stud on the lower left of each supply's own face, below its two status lamps. Neither ufispace/psu-302-dc@1 nor ufispace/psu-302-ac@1 contracts that stud - they were built from the S9321-64E, whose figures do not show it - and those components are shared with another platform, so it is recorded here rather than added to them from this device's evidence alone.
gaps.wanted: a straight-on elevation or photograph of a PSU-302 face at a stated scale

gaps.note: No held figure shows an AC build seated in this chassis. HIG Figure 4's rear elevation and the vendor rear render both draw the DC supply, so the `ac` configuration swaps in a contract whose own face was measured on the S9321-64E and not here. The bay geometry is identical (68 x 40.6 in both guides' tables), so what is unverified is the face artwork, not the fit.
gaps.wanted: a rear photograph or elevation of an AC-configured S9611-36D

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9611-36D, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and the one fan. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs for the AC and DC builds almost certainly exist. The configurations therefore carry no part numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide or a quote naming the chassis SKUs

gaps.note: The HIG counts the rail attachment pins ('5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins') and the locking screws ('two M4 screws, one on each chassis side') and draws them in Figure 15 without a single dimension; no held figure shows the underside at all. The five pins are therefore spread evenly along the 762 mm depth and the compliance sticker is placed by eye - every position on the left, right and bottom faces is estimated, and it is the estimates on those three faces that keep this device out of `verified`.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of either side wall, or a photograph of the underside

artwork-model-name.note: EVERY HELD FIGURE OF THIS FACEPLATE PRINTS 'S9610-36D', NOT 'S9611-36D'. That is true of the S9611-36D HIG's own port-overview figures (fig-0015 to fig-0018), of the S9611-36D datasheet's front and rear views (fig-0003, fig-0004) and of all three vendor renders. The two are a near-twin pair on one mechanical platform and UfiSpace has illustrated this guide with the sibling's artwork. The silkscreen here prints S9611-36D, because a drawing of an S9611-36D that letters it as a different product would be wrong in the one place a reader looks to identify the box - but that is the ONE mark on this model taken from reasoning rather than from the artwork, and it is recorded as the artwork-model-name gap rather than passed off as read. Everything else on this face is measured from those same figures, which is sound: the guide is the S9611-36D's own and its dimensions, LED table, port table and callouts are all written for the S9611-36D.

attrs.note: datasheet - Key Features, Specifications, Environmental, Performance, Regulatory Compliance and Supported Accessories, transcribed into sections; timing profile list and the two asterisked qualifiers kept verbatim. Compliance strings kept semicolon-separated and untidied. The datasheet prints no Safety row content beyond UL/IEC 62368-1 and no NEBS claim, and none is invented; the HIG's section 13 does carry NEBS compliance statements, which is recorded as such and not upgraded to a certification.

chassis.note: datasheet - 'Chassis (WxDxH) 2RU, 436 x 762 x 87.7 mm or 17.17' x 30' x 3.45'', 'Weight: 24.12kg or 53.18lb (without FRU)'; the HIG's Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple ('S9611-36D (W x D x H) 17.16' x 30' x 3.45' (436 x 762 x 87.7mm)') and the same weight. 436 is the body between the ear planes and not a rack face: the front render draws two small bracket studs standing OUTSIDE the full-height body on each side (px 0-9 and 1678-1687 against a body of 10-1677), and that mounting hardware is not drawn here. 87.7 mm is 1.98 rack units, which is why the datasheet calls it 2RU. Panel grey is sampled off the front render at rgb(71,71,71).

connector-identity.note: photo/drawing, and settled by two marks rather than by position. The ganged housing holds three connectors: the UPPER RJ45 carries two integrated green lamps in its top corners and the network symbol above it, so it is the 100/1000M out-of-band port; the LOWER RJ45 carries no lamps and has the IOIOI serial mark printed under the housing, so it is the RS-232 console; the blue socket between them is the USB 3.0 Type-A, marked with the SuperSpeed glyph. The micro-USB at the foot of the left column has its own IOIOI mark and is the second serial console, which matches the HIG's 'the console can be connected either with the IOIO port or the micro USB port' and the Micro USB Cable in the accessory list. HIG Figure 4's callouts label both jacks only 'RJ45' and would not have separated them.

connector-orientation.note: checked in an 11x crop rather than assumed, and this is the one thing the first render got backwards. The two RJ45s MIRROR: the UPPER jack's latch keyway is a notch at the TOP of its aperture, with its two green lamps in the upper corners and its eight contacts in the lower half; the LOWER jack's keyway is at the BOTTOM and its contacts are at the top. std/rj45-ganged draws contacts at the top and the keyway at the bottom, so the OOB jack is rotate: 180 and the CONSOLE jack is unrotated - which is the opposite way round from the S9311-64D and is why it was worth zooming. std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11) is used rather than std/rj45 (16 mm bezel) because the housing's interior aperture measures 12.0 mm across and 10.4 tall, which a 16 mm bezel cannot sit in. The stacked SFP+ pair mirrors the same way - the upper cage's latch tab hangs into the strip BELOW it and the lower cage's into the strip ABOVE - and std/sfp-ganged draws its cage lip at the bottom of an upright opening, so sfp-0 is unrotated and sfp-1 is rotate: 180. The USB 3.0 socket is LANDSCAPE here (aperture 12.0 wide by 5.5 tall), unlike the S9311-64D's portrait one, so std/usb-a is placed unrotated.

front-layout.note: drawing - the vendor front elevation at 3.8257 px/mm across and 3.8427 down, cross-checked against HIG Figures 8-11 (which are the same artwork at 2.7 px/mm) and against the datasheet's own front view. Left to right: a management column at the left edge (a blind boss and the RESET pinhole, the model name, the two-digit beacon display, two unnamed slots, an unnamed mesh window and a second blind boss, the 1PPS and 10MHz SMB jacks, and the five system lamps against their printed legend block, with the micro-USB console at the foot), then a three-high ganged silver housing carrying the OOB RJ45 over the USB 3.0 socket over the console RJ45, then the stacked SFP+ pair, then the eighteen QSFP-DD columns in five blocks of 2, 4, 4, 4 and 4. Positions read off that render are good to about 0.3 mm and are carried as drawing confidence. The narrow dark recess at x 432.9-435.5, y 35.4-65.3 in the blank right margin is drawn because two independent images show it in the same place, and is drawn as decor rather than as a part because nothing in any held document names it - it reads as a finger pull for sliding the chassis on its rails, and that reading is a guess. The S9311-64D carries the same feature at 432.3-434.9, y 33.9-64.2, which is corroboration of the family idiom and not of this measurement.

ganged-housing.note: drawing - the bright metal frame around the three stacked connectors is PANEL, not part: std/rj45-ganged and std/usb-a draw their apertures and stop, and without the frame three dark connectors on a dark faceplate are invisible. It is drawn as a panel.decor fill at x 18.82-35.03, y 46.32-78.07, measured from the frame's own outer edge (px 82-144, 178-300) - the flange as it shows on the outside of the panel, not the connector body behind it.

grounding.note: HIG section 8 - the router 'can be grounded from the router's case and/or the power supply units', with a two-hole #4 AWG lug and two M4 screws, and 'the location for securing the grounding lug is at the rear of the case and is covered with a protective label'. Figure 4 calls that location out by name (Ground Lug) and both rear images draw it in the same place: a tall silver two-hole plate on the strip between the fan bank and the PSUs, with an earth symbol below it. It is drawn there as decor for the plate and its two holes plus a common/ground-symbol placement for the earth mark. The PSU-side grounding the prose also offers is a stud on the supply's own face - it is visible in both rear images and is NOT in the psu-302 contracts, so it is filed as the psu-ground-stud gap rather than drawn on the chassis.

legend-wording.note: read off the artwork at high zoom, not inferred. RESET, S9610-36D (see the artwork-model-name note), 1PPS, 10MHZ and the five legend rows SYNC / SYS / FAN / PS0 / PS1 all resolve cleanly at 3.83 px/mm with 12x magnification, and SYNC..PS1 are also exactly the five rows of the HIG's Front Panel LED table, in that order. Four glyphs are drawn as seen rather than as words: the three-box network symbol, the solid up and down triangles and the SuperSpeed USB mark above the ganged housing, the '0' up-triangle / down-triangle '1' pair above the SFP+ stack, and the IOIOI serial-console mark printed twice, once under the micro-USB and once under the housing. The HIG names that last one itself - 'the port labelled IOIO' - in section 11, which is what identifies the lower RJ45 as the RS-232 console.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9611-36D end of life' - no announcement found; the results are dominated by the sibling S9610-36D's live product pages and the vendor's aggregation-router line is current. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.

port-label-colour.note: drawing, and the colour carries information. Thirty-two of the thirty-six label strips are printed blue and four are printed amber. The amber ones are ports 1, 17, 19 and 35 - detected on the front render by colour alone, before the guide was read on the point - and HIG Figure 9 marks exactly those four as 'Ports disabled when statistics counter is enabled', which is the section's OP2 note: 'when OP2 is enabled, only the remaining 32 ports will function as service ports'. 36 minus 4 is 32, so the count, the shading and the prose agree. Two independent documents also agree on the colour itself: the datasheet's own front view (fig-0003), which is not the HIG's artwork, carries the same four amber strips in the same places. The colour is therefore recorded as printed rather than as a figure highlight.

port-labels.note: drawing - and these ARE printed on the metal, which is why they are drawn here and were not on the S9311-64D. Each pair of columns carries a four-part cluster in the gutter between them, above the upper row and again below the lower: a coloured label strip with a solid triangle pointing at the column it names, a round green lamp, and a second coloured strip carrying that port's number. The left column's triangle points LEFT and the right column's points RIGHT, so each of the 36 lamps and numerals belongs to exactly one port and the `for:` links are read off the artwork rather than inferred from adjacency. Label strips measure 2.55 x 3.40 mm; the lamps are 2.45 mm across on a 3.43-3.54 mm row pitch, which is why common/led-dot (2.0) is used and not common/led-rect (4.6 x 2.6) - led-rect would overlap its neighbour. Triangles are drawn as `path:` marks rather than as U+25C0/U+25B6, which rasterise as empty boxes.

power.note: four figures, three scopes, no conflict. The datasheet gives 'Typical power: 767 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, which is why power-envelope is bare. The HIG's Connecting Power section gives the maximum FOUR times, once per build and per optics population: DC 1752 W 'under 400G optics MSA standards' and 2073 W 'with Open ZR+ transceivers', AC 1728 W and 2049 W the same way. Those are different scopes rather than different readings, so power-max-w carries the highest, 2073, because max means the highest, and all four are recorded here. The vendor's figures are NOT reconciled against the modelled module set: the fans publish no draw at all (see the L27/L29 warnings this device carries), so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor. PSU rating 3000 W per supply from the datasheet's ordering lines ('PSU-302-DESR, 3000W DC', 'PSU-302-AESR, 3000W AC'), which is also the rating on the reused contracts.

qsfp-layout.note: drawing - eighteen columns on a 19.01 mm pitch, in five blocks whose left edges measure 60.38 / 104.29 / 186.37 / 268.19 / 350.27 mm, with block gaps of 5.9 to 6.0 mm; the last column's right edge lands at 426.31 of 436. The pitch is taken from the drawn APERTURE edges (dark runs 68-69 px wide repeating every 73 px) and NOT from any filled module face, and it is confirmed by a feature that repeats once per PAIR of ports and was detected independently: the nine green lamp columns come out at 79.33 / 123.32 / 161.20 / 205.21 / 243.22 / 287.21 / 325.22 / 369.19 / 407.22 mm, against 79.39 / 123.30 / 161.32 / 205.38 / 243.40 / 287.20 / 325.22 / 369.28 / 407.30 predicted by the block model - agreeing to 0.17 mm anywhere across 436 mm. Two rows, cage tops 51.40 and 66.05, from the bright cage-frame edges at px y 197/237 and 253/293 (row pitch 14.65 mm). Unlike the S9311-64D, whose bands are 2-high stacked cages with a perforated EMI strip running between the two apertures, every aperture here profiles uniformly black with no internal lip, so the artwork shows no asymmetry that settles which way either row faces. The lower row is therefore rotate: 180 by the library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S3: upper rotate 0 over lower 180, both bails outward) - the rule, not a reading of this artwork, and a photograph that shows otherwise overturns it. The numbering is HIG Figure 8's and is certain: even numbers on the upper row and odd on the lower, left to right, 0-35.

rear-build.note: THE DOCUMENTED BUILD IS DC AND THAT IS WHAT THE BASE CONFIGURATION SEATS. HIG Figure 4's rear elevation and the vendor rear render both draw a supply with a two-stud screw terminal block under a cover, a ground stud and a hex-perforated vent field - that is PSU-302-DESR, and HIG Figure 6 dimensions it. The AC unit exists and is orderable (PSU-302-AESR, HIG Figure 5, C20 inlet) and no held figure shows one seated in this chassis, so it is offered as the `ac` configuration and nothing about the chassis is measured from it. ufispace/psu-302-dc@1 and ufispace/psu-302-ac@1 are reused unchanged from the S9321-64E family, which is the same 68 x 458.8 x 40.6 CRPS envelope and the same two-lamp FRU table.

rear-layout.note: drawing - HIG Figure 4's rear elevation at 1.4541 px/mm across, with the FRU sizes from the HIG's own Component Physical Information table doing the work the figure is too coarse for. Four fan faces run left to right from x 6.0 on an 83.7 mm pitch: the pitch is the mean of two independent readings of the module SEAMS, 121.4 px in the orthographic figure (83.5 mm) and 291.3 px in the vendor rear render (83.95 mm), which is the flat feature to measure - the red release tabs and loop handles project off the face and gave 86.9 mm, drifting in one direction across the frame, which is the tell that a projection is being measured rather than the part. The fan module itself is the table's 81 x 81.5, so a 2.7 mm chassis web is drawn between neighbours rather than the modules being stretched to their pitch. Then the grounding strip at 345-357, then the two PSU bays stacked at x 360.3, 68 wide (the table's 68 x 40.6), on a 42.5 mm vertical pitch. The right-hand 6 mm strip carries the vendor's rotated PSU0 and PSU1 position keys. Those legends and the FAN 0 1 2 3 key under the ground point are chassis silkscreen: which bay is 0 is a position fact and cannot live on an interchangeable FRU. The two rotated labels are set at font-size 1.4 rather than the ~2.4 the artwork looks like, because L21 and L44 measure a mark's extent as if it were horizontal; the positions are the measured ones and only the type size is a concession.

smb-jacks.note: drawing - the two timing jacks are ROUND with a knurled gold nut 7.76 mm across, on centres (9.02, 42.97) and (9.02, 56.91). common/smb-jack was NOT used even though it is the library's panel SMB jack: it draws a HEX nut, which is the S9510-28DC's hardware and not this one's. The jack is therefore std/smb (the 4.83 mm registry bore, round) on a gold decor disc for the nut, which is the construction the S9311-64D uses for the same hardware.

sources.note: UfiSpace S9611-36D datasheet for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9611-36D Hardware Installation Guide (s9611-36d-hig) for the overview, PSU, fan and port figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables, the rack-mount pin count, grounding and the AC/DC system maxima; three vendor renders (photos/s9611-36d-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts, construction and - for the front - geometry, because that render passes the aspect gate. FIGURE QUALITY WAS GATED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS MEASURED. The vendor FRONT render (s9611-36d-2-front.png) has a body of 1668 x 337 px between the ear tabs against the datasheet's 436 x 87.7 mm - aspect 4.950 against a true 4.9715, 0.43% out - so it is orthographic and is the front ruler at 3.8257 px/mm across and 3.8427 down; the QSFP-DD column pitch it gives is 19.01 mm against the MSA cage's 19.0, which is the scale confirming itself on a part it did not set. HIG Figure 4's REAR elevation (the lower-right panel of fig-0010) measures 634 x 128 px, aspect 4.953 against 4.9715, 0.37% out, and is the rear ruler at 1.4541 / 1.4595 px/mm - coarse at 0.7 mm per pixel, so it is used for block boundaries and not for detail. HIG Figure 4's TOP-view footprint (the left panel of fig-0010) measures 373 x 653 px against 436 x 762 mm, aspect 0.5712 against a true 0.5722, 0.17% out, and is the top ruler at 0.8555 / 0.8570 px/mm. The REAR render is NOT orthographic - it shows the lid, so it is perspective - and was used for counts, colour and the fan seams only, with every rear dimension taken from the orthographic figure or from the vendor's own FRU table.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention (docs/pluggables-3d-design.md, S1-S4): a row pair is the upper cage upright (rotate 0) over the lower turned 180, so both cage lips face the band between the two cages and both bails face outward. Decided by the reading of the cages recorded in this provenance: the 1 SFP pair (sfp-0/sfp-1). Decided by the rule, not an observation, so a photograph of the stack overturns it: the 18 QSFP-DD pairs (port-0/port-1 to port-34/port-35). 1 of these were drawn with the upper cage turned before the std cage art moved its lip to the bottom of the opening; turning them keeps the lips in the middle band where they were drawn and seats every optic bail-outward. The QSFP-DD apertures profile uniformly black with no internal lip, so the artwork settles nothing and the question is open.

system-lamps.note: drawing - five lamps, not six: the HIG's Front Panel LED table has exactly five rows (SYNC, SYS, FAN, PS0, PS1) and the artwork prints five green dots against a five-row white legend block. There is no ID beacon lamp on this platform; the beacon is the two-digit numeric display at the top of the column, which HIG Figure 4's callout list names 'Beacon LED'. The lamps sit to the LEFT of their legend rows on a 2.51 mm pitch at x 10.77, y 63.89 / 66.47 / 69.02 / 71.43 / 73.93; the legend block is a white printed panel at x 12.55-17.25, y 62.98-74.69. Every state vocabulary is the HIG table's, transcribed row for row.

unnamed-front-features.note: three features on the left column are drawn and named by nothing. Two shallow round blind bosses (x 5.78-9.59 y 7.16-10.85, and x 12.31-15.89 y 29.17-32.74) and a small textured square window (x 7.08-10.24, y 29.17-32.63), plus a pair of short rounded slots under the display (x 6.79-10.45 and 12.02-15.68, y 24.72-26.28). They appear in the HIG figures, in the datasheet front view and in the angle render at matching proportions, so they are on the metal; HIG Figure 4's callout list names Reset, Beacon LED, 1PPS, 10MHz, USB, Micro USB, RJ45, System LED and 2 x SFP and stops. They are therefore drawn as decor and carry no part identity - see the unnamed-front-features gap.

vent-islands.note: derived - a vent field is a perforation and the drawing said so, but the marks printed inside one were floating on air (L64). The vendor interrupts the perforation where it prints, so each of those marks now has a solid patch under it in the chassis colour, drawn over the vent the way ufispace/s9600-72xc paints its port bands over one. The patch is the printing's own footprint plus 0.4 mm, which is what the S9610-36D's front render measures: its slots stop 0.4 mm outside each lamp cluster and resume 0.4 mm past it. Where a vent is simply measured wider than the metal it reaches, this states the metal that the printing proves is there without re-measuring the field.

views.note: Six views, all with drawn content. TOP: y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and per HIG Figure 4's own footprint drawing, which prints the red fan handles at the top of the panel and the front bezel screws at the bottom; six long stadium ribs run across the lid on a 104.7 mm pitch (measured pair-by-pair off the figure's rib outlines at 0.857 px/mm), three small bosses sit near the rear, and five screw heads run along the front edge. BOTTOM mirrors left-right and carries the compliance sticker at an ESTIMATED position - no held figure shows the underside. LEFT (x = 0 is the REAR) and RIGHT (x = 0 is the FRONT): each side carries the five rail attachment pins the HIG counts ('The chassis has 5 attachment pins on each side, for a total of 10 pins') plus the M4 screw that locks the inner rail ('two M4 screws, one on each chassis side'). HIG Figure 15 draws the pins numbered 1-5 front to back and the screw hole (a) beyond pin 5 at the REAR, while the sentence above it says the locking screw 'is positioned at the front of the chassis' - that sentence is about which way round the rail goes, so the screw is placed at the rear with the pins as the figure draws them. The figure dimensions none of them, so EVERY position on both side faces is estimated. Both side faces carry only symmetric content, so the depth-axis conventions are stated here rather than being exposed by an asymmetric feature.
